hero.lead: A nation of 6.0 million with farmland across two thirds of its land and eight tenths of its power renewable, with public debt of 27.4% of GDP.

capital.heading: Clean power and low debt, and incomes to match.

record.text: EU recovery and resilience grants under the plan approved in July 2021; the Commission authorised the fifth instalment on 24 July 2026
Target for domestic government bond issuance in 2026, at market value, kept in June 2026, with up to DKK 10 billion of green bonds
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Government bond issuance programme, 2026
register.detail: Danmarks Nationalbank, for the Ministry of Finance · borrowing strategy for the second half of 2026, 25 June 2026 · DKK 34.7bn issued by auctions and tap sales to the end of June · green bonds up to DKK 10bn
register.note: The target for domestic government bond issuance, at market value, kept unchanged for the second half of 2026
register.text: Danmarks Nationalbank manages central government borrowing on behalf of the Minister of Finance and kept the 2026 target for domestic government bond issuance at DKK 65 billion at market value. Green bonds of up to DKK 10 billion in proceeds are planned for 2026, allocated to eligible green expenditures of 2025.

register.name: Green government bond under the European Green Bond Standard (DGB 2.25% 2035G)
register.detail: Danmarks Nationalbank · issued 23 September 2025 · due 15 November 2035 · coupon 2.25% · greenium of 1.5 basis points
register.note: The first green government bond issued under the European Green Bond Standard
register.text: A ten-year green government bond of DKK 7 billion nominal, issued under the European Green Bond Standard. Its proceeds refinance expenditure on sustainable land use, renewable energy and clean transportation; the renewable energy serves the energy standard with clean power.

register.name: Social housing renovation framework, Landsbyggefonden, 2020–2026
register.detail: Minister for Social Affairs and Housing · answer to the Housing Committee, question 95 (corrected 11 September 2025) · DKK 2.2bn a year in 2019 prices for 2022–2026 · about DKK 2.4bn in 2025 prices in each of 2025 and 2026
register.note: The whole framework, in 2019 prices for 2020–2026; a new framework is to be negotiated for the years after 2026
register.text: The framework of Landsbyggefonden, the fund of Denmark’s social housing sector, for the renovation of social housing in 2020–2026. About DKK 4.4 billion in 2019 prices remained for 2025 and 2026, about DKK 2.4 billion in 2025 prices in each year; it serves the shelter standard for the tenants of social housing.
by: Ministry of Social Affairs and Housing

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · Recovery and Resilience Facility · grants €1,625,890,885, no loans · Council implementing decision of 13 July 2021 · fifth instalment authorised 24 July 2026
register.note: The plan is worth €1,812 million with national resources, as the Commission states it; all milestones and targets were due by August 2026
register.text: EU grants under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Denmark, paid in instalments against milestones and targets; 69% of the plan supports climate objectives. Its measures include energy efficiency in households, which serves the energy and shelter standards, and healthcare services for people on the margins of society, which serve the health standard.

register.name: Social inclusion call, European Social Fund Plus, 2026
register.detail: Danish Board of Business Development · investment memo of 26 January 2026 · call expected March 2026 · applications due August 2026 · recommendations to the board expected 5 November 2026
register.note: Up to DKK 79.4 million in the 2026 investment plan; 400 unemployed people from the margins of the labour market expected to find jobs
register.text: European Social Fund Plus money set aside in the 2026 investment plan to help small and medium-sized firms that lack workers hire unemployed people from the margins of the labour market. The memo expects 300 firms to take part, 400 people to find jobs and 300 of them to stay in work for at least three months; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: European Social Fund Plus, 2021–2027
register.detail: European Commission · Partnership Agreement with Denmark adopted, news of 30 May 2022 · part of a €808M cohesion policy strategy for 2021–2027
register.note: Skills, an inclusive labour market and support for people on the margins of the labour market
register.text: The European Social Fund Plus share of Denmark’s €808 million cohesion policy strategy for 2021–2027. It funds vocational training and higher education and supports people on the margins of the labour market, including by promoting social integration and combatting homelessness; it serves the livelihood and education standards.

register.name: Sindal Biogas expansion
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · signed loan dated 4 August 2026 · announced 5 August 2026 · 13 years · about €24.5M
register.note: To double biomethane output from 22 to 44 million Nm³ a year
register.text: A 13-year NIB loan to Sindal Biogas A/S to expand its plant in Sindal, doubling its output of biomethane from 22 to 44 million normal cubic metres a year, with the possible addition of carbon capture. It serves the energy standard with renewable gas.

register.name: Pan-EU wind power guarantee package (Danske Bank)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240611 · signed 10 July 2026 · guarantees for advance payments and performance bonds · total cost about €4,000M
register.note: Guarantee cover for wind equipment manufacturers in the EU, not a loan; not limited to Denmark
register.text: An EIB package with Danske Bank that provides guarantees for advance payments and performance bonds linked to the supply contracts of wind equipment manufacturers in the EU, including grid interconnector infrastructure. It supports the supply of clean power, part of the energy standard.

register.name: Loan for small businesses, Ringkjøbing Landbobank (II)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20260127 · signed 9 July 2026 · SMEs and mid-caps in Denmark · climate action window
register.note: At least 15% of the resulting investments are expected to go to climate action; mid-caps limited to 30%
register.text: An EIB loan to Ringkjøbing Landbobank for on-lending to small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps, mainly in Denmark, to improve their access to finance, with a window for climate action and environmental sustainability. It serves the livelihood standard through the firms that employ Danes.

register.name: Environmental projects and small businesses, Ringkjøbing Landbobank
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 26 June 2026 · 10 years · on-lending to environmental projects, SMEs and small mid-caps
register.note: At least 50% of the loan funds go to eligible environmental projects, such as wind, solar and biogas
register.text: A ten-year NIB loan to Ringkjøbing Landbobank for on-lending to environmental projects, small and medium-sized enterprises and small mid-cap companies in Denmark. It serves the livelihood standard through small businesses and the energy standard through renewable power.

register.name: Battery storage at Solar Park Kvosted
register.detail: Nordic Investment Bank · announced 11 February 2026 · 11 years · 50 MW/200 MWh · Viborg Municipality · InvestEU
register.note: Adds storage to an existing 100 MWp solar park, making it a hybrid plant
register.text: An 11-year NIB loan to Solar Park Kvosted for a 50 MW/200 MWh battery energy storage system at its 100 MWp solar park in Viborg Municipality, Central Jutland, supported by the InvestEU programme. It serves the energy standard by storing solar power for the grid.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Rolling farmland in Denmark: golden grain fields, green strips and hedgerows, with a farmhouse in the distance.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: Wind turbines along the coast of Denmark, with high-voltage power lines crossing green coastal land.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A cobbled street of colourful townhouses in Copenhagen, Denmark, with cyclists in the distance.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: A beech forest in Denmark in spring, with a woodland path under a fresh green canopy.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A river winding through reed beds and green meadows into a lake in Denmark.

items.name: Specialisterne
items.text: A social enterprise founded in Denmark in 2004 that assesses, trains and places autistic and other neurodivergent people in jobs, and helps companies build workplaces that suit them. More than 10,000 neurodivergent people have been hired through its work, which now reaches twenty-six countries; it keeps an office in Denmark.

items.name: Væksthuset
items.text: A social enterprise and commercial foundation that works with people far from the labour market to bring them into jobs or education, and invests its surplus in research and development of employment work. Under framework agreements with the City of Copenhagen for 2024–2025 it ran programmes for vulnerable young people and adults, with hybrid internships and paid hours.

items.name: Hus Forbi
items.text: A street newspaper sold by homeless people, who earn 25 kroner on each copy they sell; seven in ten sales are now paid by MobilePay. Under an agreement of May 2025 sellers receive a tax deduction of DKK 42,766, so that they do not pay tax on their sales.

items.name: Gladteknik
items.text: An IT company that creates work and community for people with disabilities. It received the disability prize of the Minister for Social Affairs and Housing on 3 December 2025, the International Day of Persons with Disabilities.

items.name: FødevareBanken
items.text: A food bank that has worked since 2008 to cut food waste by passing surplus food from the food industry on to social organisations that serve meals to people in vulnerable situations. In 2025 it counted 6.5 million meals and 487 social recipient organisations, and with Salling Group it launched MadPlus, which collects surplus food from 520 Netto, føtex and Bilka stores.
